title: Krk Prices and Realistic 2027 Budget Guide
metaDescription: Krk, Croatia prices for 2027: nightly rates, meals, ferries and car costs, with daily budgets for budget, mid-range and comfort travelers.
content:
## How Much Have Prices in Krk Changed?

Krk prices have moved up steadily since Croatia adopted the euro in 2023. Accommodation has risen the most. Restaurant prices have risen more slowly, and a main course at a standard restaurant is still around €12–25. The bridge to the mainland has been free since 15 June 2020, so reaching the island by car costs nothing in tolls for the crossing itself.

The 2026 figures below are the base for 2027. A cautious planning assumption is a 3–6% rise on accommodation and eating out. Ferry tariffs and public prices tend to change less, but they are usually revised each year.

## Quick Budget Summary for 2027

| Style | Per person per day (excluding flights) |
|---|---|
| Budget | €50–80 |
| Mid-range | €90–160 |
| Comfort | €220+ |

These figures assume two people sharing a room. Solo travelers pay more per head, because most Krk rooms are priced per unit and not per bed.

## Accommodation Prices in Krk

Accommodation takes 45–60% of a typical budget.

### Apartments and private rooms

A simple studio or one-bedroom apartment away from the seafront costs about €50–90 per night. A modern two-bedroom apartment near the coast with a balcony or sea view runs about €90–180. Mid-range apartments cost roughly €70–150 in May, June and September, and €120–180 in July and August.

Small studios in the old town of Krk Town, such as a 40 m² four-star studio near the seafront, are advertised at roughly €44–66 per person per night for two guests in 2026. Budget about €50–70 per person for 2027 in peak weeks.

### Hotels

Average hotel prices vary widely by star rating:

- 3-star hotels: about €60–150 per night depending on season. Hotel Bor in Krk Town sits about 30 m from the sea among pine trees and was renovated in 2019.
- 4-star hotels: about €110–200. Hotel Dražica in Baška is around 100 m from the beach.
- Boutique hotels in the old town: Hotel Marina is an adults-only property on the harbor with only 10 rooms and rates near €210 in season. Boutique Hotel Placa is in the pedestrian zone, about 300 m from the nearest beach.
- Larger resorts such as Sunny Krk by Valamar (194 rooms) are priced from about €150 in season.
- Luxury options in Malinska and Krk Town: €200–400+.

Cheap hostel-style beds are rare on Krk. Expect €30–45 for a basic off-season room.

### Seasonal pattern

Prices peak from mid-July to the end of August. June and September are typically 25–40% cheaper with warm sea and lighter crowds. Krk Town hotels and apartments from October to April are cheapest, but many seasonal restaurants and boat trips close.

## Food and Drink Costs

- Budget restaurant meal: about €7–12
- Main course at a mid-range restaurant: €12–25
- Dinner for two at a mid-range restaurant: about €31–60 before drinks
- Fish by weight (konoba grilled fish): often €60–90 per kilogram, so a shared fish for two commonly reaches €50–70
- Coffee: €1.80–2.80; beer: €3–4.50

A realistic daily food budget is €25–35 for budget travel, €45–70 for mid-range, and €90+ for restaurant-focused trips. Supermarkets such as those in Krk Town and Punat keep self-catering affordable. A bakery breakfast and a market lunch costs under €10.

Krk's local specialties are šurlice (hand-rolled pasta), Krk prosciutto, and Žlahtina white wine from the Vrbnik area. Ordering house wine by the glass or carafe is far cheaper than a bottle from the list.

## Transport Costs

### Getting to Krk

Krk is reached by road over the Krk Bridge. Rijeka Airport is on the island, near Omišalj. Most budget visitors arrive by bus from Rijeka or by car.

### Car and fuel

Compact car rental costs about €30–60 per day, higher in August. A car is the most practical way to visit Baška, Vrbnik and Malinska, since public buses between the towns are sparse outside July and August. Parking in Krk Town in summer is paid; budget €1–2 per hour in central zones.

### Ferries from Krk

The 2026 public tariffs are the best guide for 2027:

- Valbiska to Merag (Cres), line 332: 25 minutes, €4.40 per adult, €20.70 for a standard car. This price applies all year.
- Valbiska to Lopar (Rab), line 338: about 80 minutes. From 29 May to 27 September, an adult pays €6.20 and a standard car €33.30. Off-season it falls to €4.80 and €20.40.
- Baška to Lopar catamaran (line 323): €10 for a foot passenger, around 30 minutes, with limited daily sailings.

Car fares and passenger fares are charged separately. A family of four with a car crossing to Rab in July pays about €58 one way.

## Activities and Extras

- Half-day boat tour: €35–60
- Boat or kayak rental: €15–30 per hour for kayaks, with small motorboats more
- Beach chair and umbrella: typically €10–25 per day at organized beaches
- Many pebble beaches around Krk Town and Baška are free
- The old-town sights in Krk Town, including the Frankopan Castle exterior and the Cathedral Square, are free to walk through

Tourist tax (boravišna pristojba) is added to accommodation bills. It is generally €1.50–2.00 per person per night in high season, so a week costs about €10–14 per person.

## Sample 2027 Daily Budgets (Per Person, Two Sharing)

### Budget traveler: €50–80

Studio or private room in peak season at €25–45 per person, groceries and one cheap restaurant meal €25, bus or walking €5, free beaches. Works best in June or September.

### Mid-range traveler: €90–160

Apartment or 3-star hotel at €45–80 per person, restaurant lunch or dinner €35–50, car share €15–25, one paid activity every few days.

### Comfort traveler: €220+

A 4-star hotel or boutique room at €100–200 per person, fish dinners and wine, rented boat or private tour.

## Local Tips to Cut Costs

1. Choose June or the first half of September. Rooms are often 25–40% cheaper than in August with the same weather.
2. Stay a few kilometers outside Krk Town in places such as Punat or Malinska, where apartment prices can drop by €15–30 per night.
3. Eat the main meal at lunch. Many konobas have a daily plate or a set menu priced below dinner rates.
4. Check whether a booking includes parking. Old-town rooms often do not, and Krk Town's central lots fill quickly in July.
5. Book August stays by February to March. The best-value apartments go first.
6. Buy ferry tickets on the day for the Merag crossing unless traveling on a peak weekend, when queues form at Valbiska.

The adults-only boutique hotels in the old town are usually not worth the extra cost over a well-located apartment, especially for travelers who plan to spend the day on a beach or boat anyway.

## FAQ Summary

See the questions below for quick answers on daily costs, the cheapest months and what is free.

faq.question: How much does a day in Krk cost in 2027?
faq.answer: Plan on €50–80 per person for a budget trip, €90–160 for mid-range, and €220 or more for comfort, excluding flights. These assume two people sharing a room and are based on 2026 prices with a modest increase.

faq.question: Is Krk expensive compared with other Croatian islands?
faq.answer: Krk is mid-priced. It is cheaper than Hvar or Brač in peak season, mainly because it is reachable by road without a ferry. Costs are higher than in inland Croatia, especially in July and August.

faq.question: What is the cheapest time to visit Krk in 2027?
faq.answer: October to April has the lowest prices, but many restaurants and boat trips are closed. For good weather at lower rates, June and September are the best balance, with apartments often 25–40% cheaper than August.

faq.question: How much is a meal in Krk?
faq.answer: A main course at a typical restaurant costs €12–25, and a budget meal can be €7–12. Grilled fish sold by weight is far more expensive, often €60–90 per kilogram.

faq.question: Do you need a car on Krk?
faq.answer: A car is useful for reaching Baška, Vrbnik and Malinska, and rental starts at about €30–60 per day. Krk Town itself is walkable, and you can manage a short stay there without one.

faq.question: How much is the ferry from Krk to Cres or Rab?
faq.answer: On the 2026 tariff, Valbiska to Merag (Cres) costs €4.40 per adult and €20.70 per standard car. Valbiska to Lopar (Rab) costs €6.20 per adult and €33.30 per car in high season, with lower prices off-season.

faq.question: Is it cheaper to stay in Krk Town or elsewhere on the island?
faq.answer: Smaller towns such as Punat or Malinska are often €15–30 per night cheaper than central Krk Town. Baška has strong beach access but sits at similar or higher prices in peak season.

quickAnswer: A realistic 2027 budget for Krk is about €50–80 per person per day for budget travel, €90–160 for mid-range and €220+ for comfort, excluding flights. Accommodation is the biggest cost, at roughly €120–180 per night for a mid-range apartment in July and August. Prices rise about 3–6% a year.
